newsitem.title: UK: Billiton analyst calls on IPAI to re-consider data.
newsitem.headline: Billiton analyst calls on IPAI to re-consider data.

text.p: The International Primary Aluminium Institute (IPAI) should re-consider its practice of including data from China and Tajikistan, metals analyst Angus MacMillan said.

In an open letter to the IPAI MacMillan, who is research manager at London Metal Exchange (LME) trader Billiton Metals Ltd, expressed dismay that the statistical body was continuing to include production data from these countries.
The inclusion of the new data for the first time in January's production data (isued on February 20) left some questions about crucial Chinese data unanswered, according to analysts at the time.

"When you instituted this practice without prior notice in February (reporting the January figures) you caused a furore in the market, and were warned that inclusion of data from these countries would result in confusion."
"In short, you have contaminated a sound data series, relied upon for consistency by a considerable number of people, by including data the veracity of which is widely questioned."
MacMillan said the major problem was China, where a large proportion of the country's output comes from many small plants which have capacities of less than 30,000 tonnes a year.
Neither the State Statistical Bureau (SSB) or the China National Non-ferrous Metals Industry Corp (CNNC) is in a position to collate data consistently or report it in a timely fashion.
"In any event consistency and timeliness must surely be the overriding criteria which apply when deciding what information to include in your published data series."
"As things stand neither the production nor inventory data are of value to observers of the market you (presumably) seek to serve."

"If you are unable, as you have claimed in the press, for legal reasons to publish Chinese and Tajik data separately then for the sake of clarity and statistical consistency I urge you to either cease reporting them altogether or lump them both together and call it 'Central Asia'."
The IPAI is a statistical body that reports monthly figures on aluminium production and stocks compiled from contributors worldwide.
This year, it has added data from China, Tajikistan, as well as Montenegro.
IPAI officials were not immediately available for comment.
